text.p: Turkish money market rates remained high on cash demand which emerged ahead of the weekend on Friday although the market opened seven trillion lira long, bankers said.

The central bank funded banks 26.2 trillion lira overnight at 72 percent at close and 18 trillion lira at 67 via tmrw/next. The average overnight money rate was slightly higher at 71.88 percent, compared to Thursday's 71.19 percent.
The average repo rate also rose to 73.12 percent from Thursday's 70.93 in line with the cash squeeze.
Bond yields went up by around one point across the board to 95-96 percent levels due to tight liquidity.
Another reason behind the rise in yields was political tension, bankers said. Turkish markets awaited a National Security Council meeting which began at 1310 GMT.

Top political leaders and military commanders met for talks chaired by President Suleyman Demirel and expected to focus on increasing strains between the Islamist-led government and the secular establishment.

The council, dominated by secularist officers, is likely to issue a warning to Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan that Turkey's democratic institutions are being threatened by rising Islamic zeal, political analysts said.
The most heavily traded paper was December 10, 1997 sold in Tuesday's auction. Its yield rose to 96.24 percent from 95.11 percent on Thursday. Trade volumes in other bonds were negligible.
The Turkish lira eased to 122,410 against the dollar from 122,090 at Thursday's close in line with the firmer dollar/mark parity.
